column1: # Marks (type/hide functions) and top-level expressions. Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# A REFUSED VALUE STAYS REFUSED INSIDE type() AND hide().
# Both marks walked their argument and marked it -- including when the
# argument was already an error value -- and the bag's marked-child skip
# then dropped it, so a parse-time refusal (a lossy literal, an unknown
# function, an overflowing literal) was silently swallowed and the
# document generated as if the key were absent. TypeScript returns a nil
# argument unchanged before marking, and is right: refusal over corruption.
# A REFERENCE DEFERS ON A PENDING MARK WRAPPER (ADR-005, 2026-08-26;
# use-cases/BUGS.md §11, §12, §35b). A reference that found a
# type()/hide() call still waiting for its argument used to clone the
# CALL, and the clone resolved at the reference's site, stamping marks
# after the reference's mark-clearing walk had already run. Three
# silent corruptions shared that one mechanism: hide(pack(...)) leaked
# its mark onto downstream packs over the generated children (empty
# children, exit 0); a type()-marked alias referenced inside a type()
# body suppressed the referring field's emission entirely (the
# edge.tsv edge-type-template contract extended to conjunction-bearing
# shapes); and hide() around a computed field of a pack-generated
# child swallowed the value into a silent []. The reference now
# residuates until the wrapper has resolved at its OWN field, then
# clones with marks cleared as documented. Parity-probed in both
# The referring statement WRITTEN FIRST, so the reference meets the
# alias while it is still a pending conjunct carrying the type()
# call — the shape the defer's conjunct walk exists for. Document
# order must not change the answer.
